```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Jeong_2026_sirolimus"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Jeong_2026_sirolimus"))$description`
* Article: [Br J Clin Pharmacol. 2026;92(9):3115](https://doi.org/10.1002/bcp.70595)

Jeong and colleagues pooled prospective (intensively sampled) and
retrospective (therapeutic-drug-monitoring trough) whole-blood sirolimus data
from children and adolescents with vascular anomalies and fitted a
two-compartment model with first-order absorption in NONMEM 7.5 (FOCE-I) on
log-transformed concentrations. Body size enters through allometric scaling to
70 kg, clearance maturation through a sigmoid function of postmenstrual age
(PMA) whose TM50 and Hill coefficient were fixed to literature values, and
haemoglobin through a linear effect on clearance retained after a bootstrap
stepwise covariate search. Because the pooled data could not identify every
structural parameter, the final estimation used a NONMEM `$PRIOR NWPRI` built
from the Miyazaki 2024 paediatric/adult sirolimus model.

The paper then simulated once-daily mg/kg regimens for one month in eleven
weight / PMA groups to pick, for each group, the dose that best keeps the
steady-state trough within 5-15 ng/mL (Table 3, Figure S3), and showed how
haemoglobin shifts the trough at the chosen dose (Figure 2). This vignette
reproduces both.

# Population

28 paediatric patients (11 male / 17 female) contributed 107 whole-blood
samples: 7 prospective patients gave 74 samples and 21 retrospective patients
gave the remaining 33 (Results; Table 1). Age was 8.7 +/- 5.6 years
(0.3-18.3; 4 infants, 15 children and 9 adolescents), weight 37 +/- 24.7 kg
(6.3-83.8), and haemoglobin 12.6 +/- 1.2 g/dL (10.2-14.6). Gestational age was
not recorded; PMA was derived as postnatal age + 40 weeks. Single doses ranged
from 0.27 to 1.04 mg/m^2^ or 0.01 to 0.04 mg/kg (Discussion). The same
information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Jeong_2026_sirolimus"))$population)
```

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: depot -> central <-> peripheral, first-order absorption and elimination | -- | Results ("two-compartmental model"); Figure S1 scheme |
| `lka` | 0.175 1/h | Table 2, Ka |
| `lcl` | 14.7 L/h/70 kg | Table 2, CL/F |
| `lvc` | 102 L/70 kg | Table 2, Vc/F |
| `lvp` | 725 L/70 kg | Table 2, Vp/F |
| `lq` | 24.7 L/h/70 kg | Table 2, Q/F |
| `e_wt_cl` (CL and Q) | 0.75, fixed | Results final-model equation; Figure S1 |
| `e_wt_vc` (Vc and Vp) | 1, fixed | Results final-model equation (Vc); Figure S1 (Vc and Vp) |
| `ltm50_cl` | 62.9 weeks, fixed | Table 2, TM50 |
| `lhill_cl` | 2.94, fixed | Table 2, Hill |
| Maturation `MF = PMA^Hill / (TM50^Hill + PMA^Hill)` | -- | Results final-model equation |
| `e_hgb_cl`, CL x (1 + e_hgb_cl x (HGB - 12.6)) | -0.155 per g/dL | Table 2, COVHGB; Results equation (centre 12.6) |
| `etalcl` | 0.124 (variance) | Table 2, IIV_CL/F |
| `etalvc` | 1.9 (variance) | Table 2, IIV_Vc/F; Figure S1 (eta1 on Vc) |
| `expSd` | sqrt(0.13) = 0.361 | Table 2, RV (proportional) = 0.13 on log-transformed data |
| Concentration `Cc = central / vc x 1000` (ng/mL) | -- | Units: dose mg, volume L |

# Virtual cohort

The paper generated weight and age from the 2017 Korean paediatric growth
charts. Those charts are not reproduced in the source, so this vignette draws
weight uniformly within each group's weight band and, for the infant groups,
PMA uniformly within the group's PMA band. For the groups with PMA > 144 weeks
(older than about 2 years) age is read off an approximate median
weight-for-age relationship, floored at 2.1 years; clearance maturation is at
least 92% complete at that age, so the choice moves clearance by a few percent
at most and only in the 10-20 kg group.

```{r cohort-helpers}
groups <- data.frame(
  grp = 1:11,
  label = c(
    "WT 5-10 kg, PMA 66-92 wk", "WT 5-10 kg, PMA 92-118 wk",
    "WT 10-20 kg, PMA 118-144 wk", "WT 10-20 kg, PMA >144 wk",
    "WT 20-30 kg", "WT 30-40 kg", "WT 40-50 kg", "WT 50-60 kg",
    "WT 60-70 kg", "WT 70-80 kg", "WT 80-90 kg"
  ),
  wt_lo = c(5, 5, 10, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80),
  wt_hi = c(10, 10, 20, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90),
  pma_lo = c(66, 92, 118, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA),
  pma_hi = c(92, 118, 144, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA),
  # Table 3: recommended once-daily dose at normal haemoglobin (mg/kg)
  dose_rec = c(0.08, 0.09, 0.09, 0.09, 0.08, 0.06, 0.06, 0.06, 0.08, 0.07, 0.06)
)
groups$label <- factor(groups$label, levels = groups$label)

# Approximate median weight-for-age (years, kg) used only to give the
# PMA > 144 week groups a plausible age.
wt_for_age <- data.frame(
  age = 2:18,
  wt = c(12.5, 14.5, 16.5, 18.5, 21, 23, 25.5, 28.5, 32, 36, 40, 45, 50, 55, 59, 62, 64)
)

# One row per virtual subject: weight, PMA (weeks) and group.
draw_cohort <- function(groups, n_per_cell, cells) {
  out <- tidyr::expand_grid(groups, cells, rep = seq_len(n_per_cell))
  out$WT <- stats::runif(nrow(out), out$wt_lo, out$wt_hi)
  infant <- !is.na(out$pma_lo)
  age_yr <- pmax(stats::approx(wt_for_age$wt, wt_for_age$age, out$WT, rule = 2)$y, 2.1)
  out$PAGE <- 40 + age_yr * 52.18
  out$PAGE[infant] <- stats::runif(sum(infant), out$pma_lo[infant], out$pma_hi[infant])
  out$id <- seq_len(nrow(out))
  out
}

# Once-daily dosing for one month (30 doses) with a trough sample at 720 h,
# just before the 31st dose. Doses go into `depot`; the trough is observed on
# the `central` state, where Cc is computed.
make_events <- function(cohort) {
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = cohort$id, time = 0, amt = cohort$dose * cohort$WT, evid = 1L,
    ii = 24, addl = 29L, cmt = "depot"
  )
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = cohort$id, time = 720, amt = 0, evid = 0L,
    ii = 0, addl = 0L, cmt = "central"
  )
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort, id, WT, PAGE, HGB), by = "id") |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
```

# Simulation

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Jeong_2026_sirolimus")
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260512)
set.seed(20260512)
```

## Figure S3 -- target attainment by dose and group

Figure S3 tabulates, for each of the eleven groups and each once-daily dose of
0.05-0.09 mg/kg, the percentage of simulated steady-state troughs inside 5-15
ng/mL (panel A), below 5 ng/mL (panel B) and above 15 ng/mL (panel C). The
haemoglobin effect was assessed only afterwards ("The effect of haemoglobin
levels was assessed after completing the simulations based on weight and
age"), so this simulation holds haemoglobin at the 12.6 g/dL reference, where
the haemoglobin factor is exactly 1.

```{r figS3-sim}
cohort_s3 <- draw_cohort(
  groups, n_per_cell = 200,
  cells = data.frame(dose = c(0.05, 0.06, 0.07, 0.08, 0.09))
)
cohort_s3$HGB <- 12.6
sim_s3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, make_events(cohort_s3), returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(length(unique(sim_s3$id)) == nrow(cohort_s3))

attain <- sim_s3 |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 720) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort_s3, id, grp, label, dose), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::group_by(grp, label, dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    target = 100 * mean(Cc >= 5 & Cc <= 15),
    below = 100 * mean(Cc < 5),
    above = 100 * mean(Cc > 15),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r figS3-published}
# Figure S3 panels B (below 5 ng/mL) and C (above 15 ng/mL), transcribed from
# the cell labels; an empty cell is 0%. Rows are doses 0.05-0.09 mg/kg,
# columns are groups 1-11. Panel A = 100 - B - C for every cell.
pub_below <- rbind(
  `0.05` = c(42, 58, 55, 61, 43, 36, 41, 34, 29, 30, 22),
  `0.06` = c(30, 37, 38, 39, 35, 24, 17, 16, 27, 15, 9),
  `0.07` = c(16, 32, 22, 31, 18, 16, 17, 10, 15, 12, 9),
  `0.08` = c(3, 23, 23, 19, 16, 21, 7, 4, 5, 9, 4),
  `0.09` = c(6, 10, 13, 15, 21, 10, 6, 6, 4, 0, 2)
)
pub_above <- rbind(
  `0.05` = c(2, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 3, 5, 1, 6),
  `0.06` = c(4, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 8, 5, 9, 14, 7),
  `0.07` = c(12, 6, 3, 0, 6, 10, 12, 13, 16, 12, 17),
  `0.08` = c(20, 11, 6, 14, 7, 13, 23, 20, 20, 28, 38),
  `0.09` = c(19, 16, 4, 11, 16, 22, 26, 31, 40, 45, 36)
)
pub_s3 <- tidyr::expand_grid(dose = c(0.05, 0.06, 0.07, 0.08, 0.09), grp = 1:11)
pub_s3$below_pub <- pub_below[cbind(match(sprintf("%.2f", pub_s3$dose), rownames(pub_below)), pub_s3$grp)]
pub_s3$above_pub <- pub_above[cbind(match(sprintf("%.2f", pub_s3$dose), rownames(pub_above)), pub_s3$grp)]
pub_s3$target_pub <- 100 - pub_s3$below_pub - pub_s3$above_pub

cmp_s3 <- attain |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose = round(dose, 2)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(pub_s3, by = c("dose", "grp"))
stopifnot(nrow(cmp_s3) == 55)
```

```{r figS3-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figure S3 of Jeong 2026 (panels A-C): percentage of steady-state
# troughs in, below and above the 5-15 ng/mL window. Points = simulated here;
# crosses = published cell values.
cmp_s3 |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    c(target, below, above, target_pub, below_pub, above_pub),
    names_to = c("range", "source"), names_pattern = "([a-z]+)_?(pub)?"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    source = ifelse(source == "pub", "Published (Figure S3)", "Simulated"),
    range = factor(range, c("target", "below", "above"),
      c("5-15 ng/mL", "< 5 ng/mL", "> 15 ng/mL"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(dose, value, colour = range, shape = source)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  geom_line(data = function(d) dplyr::filter(d, source == "Simulated")) +
  facet_wrap(~label, ncol = 4) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(4, 16)) +
  labs(x = "Once-daily dose (mg/kg)", y = "Subjects (%)", colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r figS3-check}
cmp_s3 |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Median difference, < 5 ng/mL (points)` = median(below - below_pub),
    `Median difference, > 15 ng/mL (points)` = median(above - above_pub),
    `90th pct abs difference, < 5 ng/mL` = unname(quantile(abs(below - below_pub), 0.9)),
    `90th pct abs difference, > 15 ng/mL` = unname(quantile(abs(above - above_pub), 0.9))
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

stopifnot(
  # Structural: a wrong clearance, volume, allometric exponent or variance
  # scale shifts every cell in the same direction by tens of points.
  abs(median(cmp_s3$below - cmp_s3$below_pub)) < 5,
  abs(median(cmp_s3$above - cmp_s3$above_pub)) < 5,
  # Envelope: the published cells come from 100 subjects each, so single
  # cells carry roughly +/-10 points of Monte Carlo noise.
  quantile(abs(cmp_s3$below - cmp_s3$below_pub), 0.9) < 20,
  quantile(abs(cmp_s3$above - cmp_s3$above_pub), 0.9) < 20
)
```

## Figure 2 -- haemoglobin effect at the recommended doses

Figure 2 shows boxplots of steady-state troughs at each group's Table 3 dose,
split into five 1-g/dL haemoglobin bands. The medians below were digitised by
the maintainers from Figure 2, calibrated on the dashed 5 and 15 ng/mL
reference lines of each panel row (accurate to roughly +/-0.4 ng/mL).

```{r fig2-sim}
cohort_f2 <- draw_cohort(groups, n_per_cell = 100, cells = data.frame(hb_bin = 10:14))
cohort_f2$dose <- cohort_f2$dose_rec
cohort_f2$HGB <- cohort_f2$hb_bin + stats::runif(nrow(cohort_f2))
sim_f2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, make_events(cohort_f2), returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(length(unique(sim_f2$id)) == nrow(cohort_f2))

trough_f2 <- sim_f2 |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 720) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort_f2, id, grp, label, hb_bin), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(hb = factor(paste0(hb_bin, "-", hb_bin + 1)))

dig_f2 <- tidyr::expand_grid(grp = 1:11, hb_bin = 10:14)
dig_f2$median_pub <- c(
  6.96, 7.86, 10.54, 11.60, 14.80, 6.25, 7.86, 9.11, 11.96, 13.39,
  6.25, 6.96, 8.21, 10.89, 13.39, 5.18, 6.25, 8.39, 10.54, 14.46,
  5.86, 6.55, 8.28, 11.38, 13.45, 4.83, 5.17, 7.24, 8.45, 9.14,
  4.83, 6.21, 7.59, 9.66, 11.03, 6.03, 6.90, 7.93, 10.69, 12.07,
  7.32, 8.57, 10.89, 12.68, 16.79, 6.61, 7.50, 10.54, 11.61, 14.29,
  5.89, 6.96, 8.39, 10.54, 13.39
)
```

```{r fig2-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7}
# Replicates Figure 2 of Jeong 2026: steady-state trough by haemoglobin band at
# each group's Table 3 dose. Red crosses = medians digitised from Figure 2.
trough_f2 |>
  ggplot(aes(hb, Cc)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_point(
    data = dplyr::left_join(dig_f2, dplyr::distinct(groups, grp, label), by = "grp") |>
      dplyr::mutate(hb = factor(paste0(hb_bin, "-", hb_bin + 1))),
    aes(y = median_pub), colour = "red", shape = 4, size = 2.5
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(5, 15), linetype = "dashed", colour = "steelblue") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 50)) +
  facet_wrap(~label, ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Haemoglobin (g/dL)", y = "Steady-state trough (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig2-check}
cmp_f2 <- trough_f2 |>
  dplyr::group_by(grp, hb_bin) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_sim = median(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dig_f2, by = c("grp", "hb_bin")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (median_sim - median_pub) / median_pub)
stopifnot(nrow(cmp_f2) == 55)

data.frame(
  `Median % difference` = median(cmp_f2$pct_diff),
  `90th pct abs % difference` = unname(quantile(abs(cmp_f2$pct_diff), 0.9)),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

stopifnot(
  abs(median(cmp_f2$pct_diff)) < 5,
  quantile(abs(cmp_f2$pct_diff), 0.9) < 30
)
```

## Haemoglobin centring: 12.6 or 12.9 g/dL?

The main-text final-model equation centres haemoglobin on 12.6 g/dL (the
cohort mean in Table 1), whereas the same equation drawn in Figure S1 uses
12.9 g/dL. Centring on 12.9 instead of 12.6 is the same as lowering every
subject's haemoglobin by 0.3 g/dL, which raises clearance by
0.155 x 0.3 = 4.65% of the reference value. Re-running the Figure 2 simulation
with that shift shows which reading reproduces the published medians.

```{r hgb-centring}
cohort_alt <- cohort_f2
cohort_alt$HGB <- cohort_alt$HGB - 0.3
sim_alt <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, make_events(cohort_alt), returnType = "data.frame")
cmp_alt <- sim_alt |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 720) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort_alt, id, grp, hb_bin), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::group_by(grp, hb_bin) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_sim = median(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dig_f2, by = c("grp", "hb_bin")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (median_sim - median_pub) / median_pub)

data.frame(
  Centring = c("12.6 g/dL (main text, packaged)", "12.9 g/dL (Figure S1)"),
  `Median % difference vs Figure 2` = c(median(cmp_f2$pct_diff), median(cmp_alt$pct_diff)),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

The 12.6 g/dL reading sits closer to the published medians; the 12.9 g/dL
reading runs systematically lower. Both readings use the same simulated
subjects, so the gap between the two rows (a few percent, as the 4.65%
clearance shift predicts) is not Monte Carlo noise.

```{r hgb-centring-check}
# The shift lowers every trough, so the 12.9 reading must sit below the 12.6
# reading on the same subjects.
stopifnot(median(cmp_alt$pct_diff) < median(cmp_f2$pct_diff))
```

# PKNCA validation

Typical-value steady-state profiles (random effects zeroed) for a
representative subject from each group at its Table 3 dose and haemoglobin
12.6 g/dL. `ss = 1` places each subject at the exact steady state.

```{r pknca-sim}
typ <- groups |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = grp,
    WT = (wt_lo + wt_hi) / 2,
    PAGE = ifelse(is.na(pma_lo),
      40 + 52.18 * pmax(stats::approx(wt_for_age$wt, wt_for_age$age, (wt_lo + wt_hi) / 2, rule = 2)$y, 2.1),
      (pma_lo + pma_hi) / 2
    ),
    HGB = 12.6,
    amt = dose_rec * WT
  )
ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = typ$id, time = 0, amt = typ$amt, evid = 1L, ii = 24, ss = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = typ$id, time = seq(0, 24, by = 0.25)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, ii = 0, ss = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(typ, id, WT, PAGE, HGB), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

# zeroRe() removes the random effects on purpose; rxode2 warns on every
# multi-subject solve without omega, so muffle that one warning only.
sim_typ <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame"),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  }
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(typ, id, label, amt), by = "id")
```

```{r pknca-run}
conc <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, label, time, Cc)
dose_df <- typ |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, label, time = 0, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | label + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | label + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 24,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  dplyr::select(label, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

nca_wide |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Group = label, `Cmax (ng/mL)` = cmax, `Tmax (h)` = tmax,
    `Ctrough (ng/mL)` = cmin, `AUC0-24 (ng*h/mL)` = auclast, `Cavg (ng/mL)` = cav
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

The paper reports no NCA, so the check is closed-form: at steady state
AUC0-tau = Dose / (CL/F), with CL/F the typical individual clearance at the
subject's weight and PMA.

```{r pknca-check}
cl_typ <- 14.7 * (typ$WT / 70)^0.75 *
  typ$PAGE^2.94 / (62.9^2.94 + typ$PAGE^2.94)
auc_ref <- data.frame(label = typ$label, auc_ref = typ$amt * 1000 / cl_typ)
chk <- dplyr::inner_join(nca_wide, auc_ref, by = "label") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (auclast - auc_ref) / auc_ref)
stopifnot(nrow(chk) == 11, all(abs(chk$pct) < 1))
# Every typical trough at the recommended dose should sit inside 5-15 ng/mL,
# which is what Table 3 claims for the median subject.
stopifnot(all(chk$cmin > 5 & chk$cmin < 15))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Variance scale.** Table 2 does not say whether the OMEGA and SIGMA
  entries are variances or standard deviations. They are read as NONMEM
  variances (the default output scale). The Figure S3 and Figure 2
  comparisons above, which depend directly on the spread of the trough
  distribution, reproduce the published percentages and medians under this
  reading. The Vc/F variance of 1.9 is large, but its tight bootstrap
  interval (1.85-1.96) reflects the informative Miyazaki 2024 prior rather
  than the 28-subject data.
* **Residual error.** Concentrations were log-transformed before fitting, so
  the "proportional" residual error is encoded as additive on the log scale
  (`lnorm(expSd)`, `expSd = sqrt(0.13)`).
* **Haemoglobin centring.** The main-text equation centres haemoglobin on
  12.6 g/dL and Figure S1 on 12.9 g/dL. The model uses 12.6 g/dL, which
  equals the Table 1 cohort mean and reproduces Figure 2 (see the comparison
  above). The linear factor `1 - 0.155 (HGB - 12.6)` would reach zero at
  HGB = 19.05 g/dL; the model should not be used outside the observed
  10.2-14.6 g/dL range.
* **Vp/F scaling.** The main-text equation does not list Vp/F; Figure S1
  scales it by (WT/70)^1, as for Vc/F, and that is what the model uses. Ka is
  not scaled.
* **Fixed maturation.** TM50 (62.9 weeks) and Hill (2.94) were fixed by the
  authors to literature values (Miyazaki 2024) and are encoded as `fixed()`.
  PMA must be supplied in weeks (postnatal age + 40 weeks when gestational
  age is unknown, as the authors assumed).
* **Virtual cohort.** The Korean growth charts used in the paper are not
  reproduced in the source; weights are uniform within each band and ages for
  the groups older than 2 years come from an approximate median
  weight-for-age curve (see Virtual cohort). For Figure S3 haemoglobin is
  held at the 12.6 g/dL reference; the paper's text implies haemoglobin was
  not varied in those runs but does not give the value.
* **Figure 1 not reproduced.** Figure 1 is a prediction- and
  variability-corrected VPC of the observed data. The individual dosing
  histories behind it are not published, so it cannot be regenerated.
* **Prior-informed estimates.** The final estimates came from a NONMEM
  `$PRIOR NWPRI` fit using the Miyazaki 2024 model as prior; the packaged
  values are the posterior estimates printed in Table 2, not the prior means.
